subject: fuaran-dotnet
$comment: This repository's claims ladder, declared as data: `proofs/README.md`'s own ladder — what is PROVED, what is only TESTED, what is ASSUMED — in a schema a tool can read, so the question does not have to be answered by reading prose and hoping two documents use the same words. A `not claimed` item is the ABSENCE of a row, never a row: `proofs/README.md` enumerates those, and enumerating them here would turn a disclaimer into a claim. Levels are the CLOSED set proved | tested | assumed | policy. Authored by hand, never generated: editing the ladder means editing this file and the README together. It is CHECKED rather than trusted by the `Proofs.Ladder` family in `src/Fuaran.UI.Idl.Tests/FStarVocabularyTests.fs`, which holds every row to this tree — a `proved` row's theorem is a top-level declaration of that name in the model it names, that model is one `proofs/check.ps1` actually checks, and every checked module carries at least one row.

$levels.proved: A theorem in a model the leg actually checks, with no assume and no admit under --report_assumes error. `evidence` names the top-level declaration, the model file, and the pin.
$levels.tested: A differential or conformance family, not a proof. `evidence` names the cases, and they must exist.
$levels.assumed: A premise the proof rests on and does not discharge. `evidence.assumption` states it in one sentence, in the terms a reader could go and check it in.
$levels.policy: The reproducibility posture the proved rows are only as good as — which prover is pinned, how many cold runs a check is, that an edited model without a re-extraction fails. Policy, not algebra: no theorem addresses it.

$hostFamily: `Proofs.Ladder` in `src/Fuaran.UI.Idl.Tests/FStarVocabularyTests.fs`, run by `proofs/check.ps1`'s host step and by this repository's ordinary gate. It checks row-to-TREE agreement and deliberately not row-to-PROSE agreement: the second is a human act, and the first is the half a check can settle. A go-red fixture sits beside the theorem clause, so a green ladder is known to be one that could have failed.

claims.claim: The ROUND TRIP over this repository's own wire vocabulary, GENERATED and COMMITTED: `rt_node` proves `dec_node (enc_node x) == Ok x` for every value of every MODELLED type — at every depth, through every list, map, optional member and omit-at-default — by one mutual induction over the family, emitted as one lemma per constructor and one per presence pattern (fuaran-core#168) so that no query carries more than one constructor's object shapes. Emitted by `FStarTarget.proofsModuleFrom` from the same walk that emits `Vocabulary.fst`, so the two files cannot be about different vocabularies, and held to a fresh generation by the `Proofs.Vocabulary` family. THE BOUNDARY, which is the load-bearing half: 'modelled' is twenty of this vocabulary's forty-three kinds, and the other twenty-three are NOT covered by this row — see `vocabulary-coverage` below and the emitted header, which names each one with its reason. It is also a theorem about the GENERATED codec and about no host's hand-written decoder.

Every input reaches exactly one of `Ok` / `Error` in the generated node decoder and never both — the exclusivity half of totality, stated as a lemma because the termination half is discharged by the definition type-checking at `Tot` and so leaves nothing to state.

The generated encoder and the generated decoder are TOTAL functions of the modelled vocabulary: both type-check at `Tot` under a declared `decreases`, so every input terminates in a value. The proof is the type-checking rather than a lemma, which is why this row names a definition — `dec_node` — and not a theorem. Termination is content here rather than a formality: the decoder descends into a child array obtained BY NAME, so nothing structural is visible at the call site and the measure has to be supplied.

Every decode combinator the generated decoder is built from reaches exactly one outcome on every input, and which one is characterised structurally — so the failure classification is exhaustive rather than merely non-empty. INHERITED BY COPY: `proofs/WireDecode.fst` is the kit's model, copied here and declared in `copies.json`, so this row is the kit's theorem re-checked in this repository's leg rather than a second statement of it.

The reference node decoder in the copied combinator model is total on an arbitrary JSON value and succeeds on exactly the well-formed documents. INHERITED BY COPY, as `decode-total` is. Note what it is about: the model's own REFERENCE node shape, not this vocabulary's kinds — the generated decoder's acceptance is `vocabulary-codec-total`'s subject and its characterisation is a named halt in `proofs/README.md`.

That the parser's absorption of object-member nulls is equivalent to erasing member nulls from the document tree the strict grammar would otherwise produce. INHERITED with the `WireDecode` copy: a copy of a model is a copy of the premises it rests on, and a ladder that took the theorems without the premises would be claiming more than the model does.

evidence.assumption: the parser's member-null fork equals erasing member nulls from the strict tree

claims.claim: WHICH KINDS THE THEOREMS ABOVE COVER, and that the answer is a computed rule rather than a list. The proof vocabulary is `FStarTarget.proofKinds` — every kind the target can express that introduces no declared type beyond the node envelope's own closure — which selects twenty of this vocabulary's forty-three kinds. The other twenty-three are of two sorts and the emitted header names each with its reason: ONE is a genuine BOUNDARY (`Tabs`, whose `activeIndex` is a `Binding<int>` omitted at the declared default `Static { value = 0 }`, and the model's numeric carriers are opaque, so there is no literal to spell that default's inner `VInt 0` with), and twenty-two are held out by a COST CONTROL a measurement could lift. It is a RULE and not a list, which is the property that matters: a kind added over types the model already carries enters at the next regeneration and re-proves itself. The measurement behind choosing this rule over the exhaustive expressible set — including what the exhaustive emission actually is — is in `proofs/README.md` under 'Coverage'. Policy rather than `proved`: it is a statement about the SCOPE of the rows above, and a scope is a claim at none of this ladder's other three levels.

Which prover is pinned, how many cold-cache runs a check is, and that a model edited without a regeneration fails the leg — the reproducibility posture the proved rows above are only as good as. Policy, not algebra: no theorem addresses it. The posture also says what the leg COSTS: each module's cold-run budget is declared in `proofs/modules.json`, measured on every run and printed beside the measurement, with an overshoot named as a warning and `check.ps1 -Strict` for a session that wants one red, and each module's time FLOOR declared beside it, which IS a gate. The numbers live there rather than in a row here, because a wall-clock budget is a claim at none of this ladder's four levels and is per module where a row is per claim. The pin itself is ONE number in the kit's repository, and this repository's copy of it is declared in `copies.json` so the sweep names it when it is behind.
